messages:
Maya Chen: quick share — ran a mixed-precision sweep across qwen-7b-v2 / mistral-7b / llama-2-7b. configs: FP8 kernel, INT8 hybrid, and a 4-bit fallback. TL;DR: FP8 wins latency for seq<=512, INT8 better for 1k+ tokens, 4-bit only safe with >=10k calibration samples. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Sam Patel: can you drop the raw numbers? p50/p95/p99 + throughput (tok/s) for each model+kernel?
Maya Chen: sure. sample run (qwen-7b-v2, seq=256, batch=4):
```
kernel: fp8_opt_v2
p50: 45ms
p95: 78ms
p99: 130ms
throughput: 1200 tok/s
cpu tail: +15% on host-side when batch>8
```
for same model seq=1024, batch=2 with int8_hybrid:
```
kernel: int8_hybrid_v1
p50: 85ms
p95: 150ms
p99: 260ms
throughput: 980 tok/s
```
Maya Chen: note: when kv-cache enabled and prefix hits are >30% we see ~10-12% additional speedup for fp8 due to shorter matmul paths. but small calibration (<=1k samples) for int4/4-bit produced visible perplexity regressions (delta ppl ~+4-8%).
Jordan Li: posted the profiling flamegraph link in thread — but quick excerpt: GPU active % went from 72% -> 89% when switching to fp8 for short sequences. however host-side memcpy and small-allocation stalls increased (explains cpu tail).
Lee Wong: re: calibration: confirmed on llama-2-7b. int4 with 2k samples -> quality drop; ramp up to 12k samples and synced sampling per-layer (stratified) reduces ppl delta to <1.2%. takeaway: calibration size and sampling strategy matter as much as quant scheme.
Sam Patel: interesting. we also saw a perf regression yesterday after kernel-swap commit `abc1234` — canary showed p99 jumps for mistral-7b in dedicated pool. infra-bot, do we have the rollback note?
infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollback triggered for `kernel-rollout/v1.9` at 2023-11-21T14:02:11Z due to p99 > 2x baseline on mistral-7b dedicated pool. Reason: sporadic enqueue stalls when batch size oscillates between 3-9.
Maya Chen: yep that's the one. root cause appears to be kernel selection thrash: runtime switched kernels based on instantaneous batch size leading to repeated kernel reloads and kv-cache invalidation overhead.
Sam Patel: proposed mitigation: add hysteresis window for kernel selection + sticky kernel per (model, seq_len_bucket, device). example config idea:
```
{kernels: [fp8_opt_v2, int8_hybrid_v1, int4_safe_v3],
selection_policy: {
  hysteresis_ms: 1000,
  min_stable_requests: 10,
  stickiness_ttl_ms: 300000
}}
```
Sam Patel: that should avoid thrash when batch oscillates during traffic bursts.
Jordan Li: also +1 on grouping by seq_len_bucket; we should prefer same-kernel if prefix KV hit rate > 20% to avoid kv-copy churn. simple rule: if kv_hit_rate > 0.2 -> prefer lower-latency kernel even if marginally slower for cold path.
Lee Wong: agree. for model-specific profiles I'll prepare recommended calibration sizes and kernel mapping for Llama/Mistral/Qwen. rough plan:
- Llama-2-7b: fp8 for seq<=512, int8_hybrid for 512-2048, int4 only for high-calib (>=12k) offline batches
- Mistral-7b: fp8 primary for seq<=768, int8 for long-form, avoid int4 in hosted
- Qwen-7b-v2: fp8 default, fallback int8_hybrid for sustained >1k token contexts
Lee Wong: will push PR with JSON profiles + perf numbers by EOD.
Maya Chen: one more datapoint — batching heuristic change (max_batch=32 -> 48) improved throughput but increased p99 for short seqs. we should tie max_batch to seq_len_bucket as well.
Sam Patel: agreed. let's schedule a quick triage tomorrow to land hysteresis and the profile PR. pinging @eng-oncall if canary needs manual watch. :eyes:
Maya Chen: thanks all — I'll attach the raw traces and calibration configs in the PR.
